messages:
anya: Quick sync — we need to finalize how Dedicated handles short bursts for pilot customers. I put together a compact operational playbook and a sample config. We need product, eng, SRE, and CS alignment by EOD Friday.

mike: TL;DR please.

anya: TL;DR: coordinated soft-spill: allow limited over-reservation with per-tenant smoothing, short carryover credits, a hard cap on spill duration, and explicit rollback gates + visible billing model.

jules: SRE note: main risk is a noisy tenant pushing pool 99th token latency. We need a two-phase mitigation: soft-throttle first (requests queued/ shed gracefully), then tenant preempt if credits exhausted or max_spill elapsed. Also require preempt test scenarios to validate cache behavior.

pat: CS perspective: pilot customers request predictable burst (20% headroom ask from one). They also want transparent billing/credits and an opt-in agreement. We'll need a concise FAQ and an opt-in template.

sara: Data check: sampled top 6 pools over 90 days. Median over-reserve spikes are <3 minutes; 95th <8 minutes. But 2 tenants caused multi-hour tails. I can provide per-tenant histograms by Wed.

anya: Proposed config (informal example):

```yaml
burst_policy:
  type: coordinated_soft_spill
  default_headroom_pct: 15
  carryover_credits_days: 7
  max_spill_minutes: 10
  smoothing_window_seconds: 60
  billing: credits_consumed
  emergency_preempt_threshold: pool_99th_latency_delta_pct: 30
```

mike: Implementation concerns: how do we avoid cache churn on preempt? If preempt evicts KV cache, tail latency might worsen. Suggest preempt chooses less-cache-sensitive workers first and prefers throttling over eviction. Need perf budget for pre-warm (~5% of pool).

jules: We'll draft a preempt selection policy: least-recently-used tenants, then opportunistic eviction on low-KV-usage workers. Add alarms on sudden KV hit-rate drop.

pat: Onboarding checklist for pilot: 1) customer signs opt-in terms (headroom, billing, rollback rights) 2) product + CS triage call to capture traffic patterns and acceptable SLO deltas 3) staged enable: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring gates.

anya: Launch gates (MVP):
- Observability: per-tenant spill events, credit burn, 95/99 latency, queue/backpressure metrics
- Reliability: automated rollback if pool-wide 99th token latency increases > 20% for 5m
- Cost: pre-warm budget capped per pool (configurable)
- Docs & CS playbook: onboarding steps, billing FAQ, incident runbook

sara: I'll produce recommended default headroom and the pilot traffic report by Wed.

jules: SRE will own chaos matrix (simulate long tails, rapid bursts, carryover exhaustion) and add tests: cache-sensitivity, soft-throttle efficacy, two-stage preempt.

mike: Estimated eng effort: core policy + scheduler changes ~3 sprints; billing hooks ~1 sprint; console + metrics ~1 sprint. Can parallelize telemetry and CS docs. Will gate behind a feature flag and pool-level canary.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag canary scheduled after RFC PR merge. :robot_face:

anya: Action items: @mike open RFC PR with config + migration notes by Tue; @sara attach pilot telemetry; @jules draft SRE test plan and chaos matrix; @pat create CS opt-in template and billing FAQ. I'll draft launch gates doc and rollout timeline.

mike: Ack. I'll aim to have the RFC up tomorrow.

pat: We'll run a dry-run with one pilot next week and validate billing flow with finance.

anya: Thanks all — quick sync tomorrow 10:00 to finalize numbers. :thumbsup:
